description: The agent must: (1) Read firmware/brake_ctrl/src/brake_ctrl_core.c and identify all 10 planted MISRA violations spanning mandatory and required categories. (2) Because Rule 21.3 (malloc) is present in a safety-critical path, emit a '⚠️ SAFETY CRITICAL' banner at the very top of the report before any violation blocks — this is a proprietary escalation rule from the SKILL.md that a generic agent will miss. (3) Format every violation using the exact proprietary block structure with ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ (U+2501 heavy horizontal) separators and the mandatory fields: Rule, Category, ASIL, Severity, Location, Non-Compliant Code, Why it violates, MISRA-Compliant Replacement, Explanation of fix. (4) Apply the escalation rule that Rule 15.1 (goto) is always classified ASIL D regardless of context. (5) Detect Brake_IRQ_Handler as an ISR (via __attribute__((interrupt)) annotation) and apply heightened memory-embedded rules to the malloc call inside it. (6) Produce a REVIEW SUMMARY table using ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── (U+2500 light horizontal, distinct character from violation separators) with Total violations, Mandatory/Required/Advisory breakdown, ASIL D/C/B/A/Not mapped breakdown, and Overall compliance status: FAIL. (7) Write the complete report to misra_audit_report.txt.
